It also carried the SRT badge, a symbol shared across many of Chrysler’s high-performance offerings. With its lightweight body and an 8.3-liter V-10 producing 509.9 HP, the car possessed the performance to compete against its international rivals.
cars.hero: The much-anticipated fixed-roof version of the supercar featured better aerodynamics and lighter weight.

cars.description: This premium compact was introduced in 2009. Although it shared its platform with the Citroën C3, it carried the DS badge and stood out with distinctive styling and a notably higher level of quality. The DS 3 Racing was a special edition released to commemorate the brand’s entry into the WRC in 2011. Developed by Citroën Racing, it featured a boost in engine output along with chassis enhancements.
cars.hero: A performance car that boasted exceptional quality and a high level of uniqueness.

cars.description: This is a wild Mustang build crafted by one of Oregon’s most respected custom shops. Everything from the rear seats to the trunk was stripped out to make room for a mid-mounted supercharged 5.4-liter V-8 from a Ford GT—an engine capable of producing up to 850.1 HP. Unveiled at SEMA 2012, the car took home the prestigious GT Award.
cars.hero: This Mustang, a 2012 GT Award Winner, possessed the heart of a Ford GT.

cars.description: Ferrari shortened the wheelbase of the 250 GT Berlinetta for sharper track handling. That change bore fruit with numerous race victories starting in 1960, including wins at the Tour de France and Nürburgring 621.4 miles. Just 162 units were built before its successor, the iconic 250 GTO, took over in 1962.
cars.hero: A predecessor to the 250 GTO, this car racked up numerous wins in the world of endurance racing.

cars.description: Back then, the line between road and race cars was thin, and the 250 GT Berlinetta embodied both worlds. The "GTO" name marked its homologation for GT racing. A tubular steel chassis supported the aluminum bodywork, optimizing both weight and rigidity. Its 3.0-liter V-12, fed by six carburetors, produced 295.9 HP. The right-hand-drive model developed for the UK performed admirably, often finishing on the podium.
cars.hero: This ultra-popular car was built to win the GT Class International Championship title.

cars.description: Derived from the 296 GTB, the 296 GT3 was a purebred race machine that shed the plug-in hybrid system of the road car, relying solely on a 600-horsepower twin-turbocharged V-6 engine. Built by world-renowned constructor Oreca, the car was crafted with meticulous precision—from chassis construction and assembly to customer support. After its debut at the 24 Hours of Spa in July 2022, it quickly demonstrated its exceptional racing prowess, achieving 100 victories in less than two years.
cars.hero: This elegant GT3 machine is also known as the "Racing Queen."

cars.description: The 296 GTB itself was a plug-in hybrid and the first Ferrari to feature a V-6 engine since the iconic Dino series. The smallest member of Ferrari’s current lineup, its beautifully sculpted body paid homage to the 250 LM of the 1960s. Power came from a mid-mounted twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 engine paired with a 123 kW electric motor, producing a combined output of 830 horsepower. Capable of accelerating from 0-62.1 mph in just 2.9 seconds and reaching 205.1 mph at full stride, the 296 GTB delivered the breathtaking performance worthy of the Ferrari name.
cars.hero: Here's a mid-engine sports car with a revolutionary V-6 + PHEV system.

cars.description: Introduced in 1975, the 308 GTB replaced the Dino 246 GT and launched Ferrari’s long-running series of V-8-powered two-seaters. Its elegant body, laid over a steel-tube frame, was designed by Leonardo Fioravanti of Pininfarina, the mind behind many of Ferrari’s most celebrated shapes from the 1960s through the early 1990s.
cars.hero: This successor to the Ferrari Dino 246 GT features a V-8 mounted amidships.

cars.description: The 330 P4 was Ferrari’s answer to the dominance of the Ford GT. Although only four units were ever made, a berlinetta version for high-speed tracks and a roofless spider for reduced weight were produced. It won its debut race at the 24 Hours of Daytona. While Ford ultimately triumphed at Le Mans, Ferrari secured the World Sportscar Championship title.
cars.hero: This V12-powered P Series race car was known as "the most beautiful machine ever."

cars.description: The 365 GTB/4—aka Daytona—was the last Ferrari to have a front-mounted V-12 and made its debut at the 1968 Paris Motor Show. It wore sleek bodywork penned by Leonardo Fioravanti, with a 4390 cc DOHC V-12 powerplant residing underneath. With a top speed of 174 mph, it matched the Lamborghini Miura as the fastest production car of its time.
cars.hero: The ultimate super sport, this front engine, rear-wheel drive machine rivaled the Miura for the highest top speed of its day.

cars.description: Revealed at the 2007 Frankfurt Motor Show in September, the Ferrari 430 Scuderia reflected the brand’s Formula 1 expertise. Compared to the base F430, it featured enhanced aerodynamics, weight reduction, and more power. The result was a 0–62.1 mph sprint in just 3.6 seconds and a top speed of 198.8 mph.
cars.hero: A road-going racer that greatly improved upon the performance of the F430.

cars.description: The 458 Italia, introduced at the 2009 Frankfurt Motor Show, succeeded the F430. Built on a new aluminum space frame, it housed a 4499 cc V-8 producing 562.1 HP and 398.5 ft-lb of torque. The upgraded Manettino system allowed seamless control of engine, transmission, and suspension settings. With F1-derived aero design, it hit 0–62.1 mph in 3.4 seconds and topped out at 201.9 mph.
cars.hero: With an astonishing 562.1 HP under the hood, this V8 mid-engine machine took its heritage from the F430.

cars.description: The 458 Gr.4 is a Gran Turismo Original entry-level race model in Ferrari’s lineup. While its aero-package was subtle, the base car’s downforce and handling remains intact. Combined with the Ferrari V-8 and 7-speed gearbox, it offers strong performance on the circuit.
cars.hero: With an astonishing 562.1 HP under the hood, this mid-engine V-8-powered machine drew its inspiration from the F430.

cars.description: The 458 Italia GT3 was a regulation-compliant race version of the road-going 458. It featured a lower front bumper functioning as an air dam and a prominent rear wing. Although the engine remained the same, a restrictor limited output to 542.4 HP. Making its debut in 2011, it immediately made its mark by winning the FIA GT3 European Championship.
cars.hero: This car, which generates more downforce than any Ferrari before it, won the FIA-GT European Championship title.

cars.description: The Ferrari 499P was a prototype developed for the Le Mans Hypercar (LMH) category. Its advanced hybrid all-wheel-drive system combined a twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 engine with a front-mounted MGU to produce a total output of 500kW. Upon Ferrari’s return to Le Mans in 2023, the car went up against a field of its strongest rivals and came out on top, securing overall victory. This would mark Ferrari’s first victory at Le Mans in 58 years.
cars.hero: The glorious Prancing Horse that returned Ferrari to the top category and delivered victory at Le Mans after a 50-year absence.

cars.description: The 500 Mondial Pinin Farina Coupe, a car built for the 1954 Tour de France, featured a chassis and engine developed by Ferrari and bodywork by Pininfarina. Although it never competed in the Tour as intended, an unrestored example later won the prestigious Gran Turismo Award at the 2012 Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance.
cars.hero: A priceless unrestored example of a Gran Turismo Award winner.

cars.description: This modified version of Ferrari’s 365 GT4/BB was notable for being the brand’s first mid-engine 12-cylinder road car. The most significant revision was the enlargement of the engine to 5.0 liters; however, due to emissions regulations, power output was reduced by 19.7 HP, bringing the total to 355 HP. Torque was increased by 28.9 ft-lb, resulting in a formidable 332.7 ft-lb. One of Ferrari’s most iconic creations, this car—along with Lamborghini’s Countach—came to symbolize the exotic Italian supercars of the 1970s.
cars.hero: One of the cars that defined the supercar boom in the 1970s, this car was considered the world's fastest, along with the Lamborghini Countach.

cars.description: The Ferrari 812 Superfast, introduced in 2017, carried on the company's tradition of front-engined V-12 grand tourers. It marked Ferrari’s first use of electric power steering and adopted an evolved version of the 4-wheel steering system from the F12berlinetta. Despite its substantial 107.1 inches wheelbase, the car remained impressively agile through tight corners.
cars.hero: Adopting the classic V-12 FR layout, this Ferrari possesses remarkable performance while retaining practicality.

cars.description: An evolution of the Dino 206GT introduced in 1968, the Dino 246GT was named in honor of Enzo Ferrari’s late son. The aluminum body was replaced with a steel construction, and the wheelbase was extended to enhance control and high-speed stability. The cast-iron block V-6 was enlarged to 2.4 liters, producing 192.3 HP and 166.4 ft-lb of torque.
cars.hero: This collector's car took the nickname of Enzo Ferrari's son, Alfredo "Dino," who passed away at the age of 24.

cars.description: This limited-production supercar, with only 399 units built, was launched in 2002 to commemorate Ferrari’s 55th anniversary. Its sharp-nosed, Formula 1-inspired design was the work of Ken (Kiyoyuki) Okuyama, then a designer at Pininfarina. The car was constructed with extensive use of carbon composites for both the body panels and much of the framework. At its heart was a specially developed 6.0-liter V-12 producing 650.9 HP and 484.6 ft-lb of torque, allowing the car to reach a top speed of more than 217.5 mph.
cars.hero: Christened with the name of the founder, this car celebrated the company's 55th anniversary and had a limited 399-production run.

cars.description: The F12berlinetta was introduced in 2012 as Ferrari’s new flagship grand tourer, succeeding the 599 GTB Fiorano. Built around an all-new aluminum space frame and body shell, it featured a front-mid-mounted V-12 engine. With its optimized layout, it accelerated from zero to 62.1 mph in just 3.1 seconds and reaching a top speed of 211.3 mph. It also claimed the lap record at Ferrari’s Fiorano test track.
cars.hero: The flagship model of Ferrari wasn't just fast, it was a technological marvel.

cars.description: This mid-engine sports car featured a Pininfarina-designed body that perfectly blended flowing lines with functional beauty. Its naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V-8 produced 107.5 HP per liter, an extraordinary achievement for its time. Its superb weight balance and cutting-edge electronically controlled suspension gave it handling that helped establish the car as one of the great masterpieces in Ferrari history.
cars.hero: A masterpiece new generation midship, that inherits the passion of the 348.

cars.description: This special model was created to commemorate the 40th anniversary of Ferrari’s founding. Developed using the same construction techniques as the race cars of its era, it featured a steel tubular frame combined with composite materials, including carbon-Kevlar and aluminum honeycomb structures. Its powerplant was derived from the twin-turbocharged V-8 used in the 288 GTO, tuned to produce 478.3 HP and 419.5 ft-lb of torque. This car would become the final road-going project overseen by Enzo Ferrari, and it continues to enjoy enduring admiration around the world.
cars.hero: This special exotic machine was the last one produced under the guidance of company founder Enzo Ferrari.

cars.description: The Ferrari F430 was a mid-engine V-8 supercar that made its debut in 2004. The newly developed 4.3-liter V-8 engine produced 483.2 HP. The chassis was developed from the 360 Modena, with key improvements in stability and aerodynamic downforce, constructed using Extra Super Duralumin aluminum alloy. This top-tier sports car reached a top speed of 195.7 mph and was available with carbon-ceramic brakes.
cars.hero: The rolling piece of mechanical art was capable of reaching a top speed of 195.7 mph.

cars.description: This special model was created to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Ferrari’s founding. Developed under the concept of a “road-going F1 car,” it featured an engine derived from the V-12 in Ferrari’s 1990 "641" F1 machine, enlarged to 4.7 liters and mounted directly to the chassis. With an output of 512.8 HP and 347.2 ft-lb of torque, the car could accelerate from zero to 62.1 mph in just 3.87 seconds and reach a top speed of 201.9 mph.
cars.hero: This Italian masterpiece, equipped with a naturally-aspirated V-12 and Formula 1 technology, celebrated Ferrari's 50th anniversary.

cars.description: The Ferrari F8 Tributo was unveiled in 2019 as the successor to the 488 GTB. While it retained a shape similar to its predecessor, significant changes to the aerodynamic elements gave it a refreshed, aggressive character. Its twin-turbo 3.9-liter V-8 produced 710.1 HP, resulting in a zero-to-62.1 mph of 2.9 seconds and a top speed of 211.3 mph—making it the fastest V-8-powered road car Ferrari had ever produced. Equipped with the latest in body control systems, the F8 Tributo also offered remarkable ease of drivability.
cars.hero: At the heart of this exotic, an update to the 488GTB, is a powerful V-8 that was also in the 488 Pista.

cars.description: The Ferrari Vision Gran Turismo marks Ferrari’s first-ever virtual-only single-seater concept, drawing design cues from the marque’s legendary sports prototypes of the 1960s and 1970s. Its turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 hybrid powertrain, working in concert with three electric motors, delivers a total system output of 1015.8 HP. Blending the DNA of Ferrari’s past icons with a bold vision of endurance racing’s future, the design is both a tribute and a statement.
cars.hero: A single-seat concept that pushes the boundaries of the hypercar genre.

cars.description: The FXX K, a track-only evolution of the LaFerrari, was produced in a limited run of just 32 units in 2014. It pairs the LaFerrari’s 6.3-liter V12 with a 187.4 HP electric motor, delivering a combined output of 1035.5 HP. With enhanced aerodynamics—further amplified by the optional EVO kit, which adds 75 percent more downforce. Free from the constraints of racing regulations, this car delivers pure, uncompromised driving performance at its highest level.
cars.hero: The production run of this Ferrari was limited to only 32 units.

cars.description: To qualify for Group B, Ferrari built 200 examples of this homologation special. Although it looked like the 308, it featured a longer wheelbase by 4.3 inches and a longitudinally mounted engine, making it mechanically distinct. The twin-turbocharged 2.8-liter V-8 delivered 394.5 HP, making it the fastest road-going Ferrari at the time.
cars.hero: At first glance, this monster car appears to be an offshoot model, but it's 100% custom-built on the inside, and produces over 394 horsepower.

cars.description: This was one of Ferrari’s flagship special models—continuing the legacy of the F40, F50, and Enzo Ferrari. It was built using the same materials and techniques found in Ferrari’s Formula 1 program, with a carbon monocoque chassis and a specially tuned version of the 6.3-liter V-12 engine from the F12berlinetta, producing 788 HP, enhanced further by the HY-KERS hybrid system. Performance was nothing short of astounding: 0–62.1 mph in under 3 seconds, 0–124.3 mph in under 7 seconds, and a top speed exceeding 217.5 mph.
cars.hero: Ferrari’s first hybrid car, built with the same materials and processes as an F1 racing machine.

cars.description: Unveiled in 1984, the Testarossa stood as Ferrari’s flagship mid-engine masterpiece. Its heart was a 5.0-liter 180-degree V-12, delivering a maximum output of 384.6 HP and torque of 361.6 ft-lb. Acceleration from zero to 62.1 mph took just 5.8 seconds, with the car ultimately achieving a top speed of 180.2 mph. With its sculpted form—defined by signature 5-fin strakes and rear fenders that flared boldly from the tight cockpit—the Testarossa captivated a new generation of enthusiasts.
cars.hero: This historic Ferrari flagship impressed all with its vivid design.

cars.description: Thanks to its affordable pricing and endearing styling, the original FIAT 500 sold more than four million units over its 20-year production run starting in 1957. Half a century after the second-generation model, the third-generation FIAT 500 arrived. Making its debut at the 2004 Geneva Motor Show, the new Fiat 500 launched to widespread acclaim in the summer of 2007. It was affectionately known around the world as the Cinquecento—Italian for “500."
cars.hero: The Italian version of the people's car makes a comeback after a 50-year hiatus.

cars.description: The car symbolized FIAT’s original mission of delivering accessible, everyday mobility. The first 500, born in 1957, featured an extremely compact body housing a 497 cc engine with just 14.8 HP, mounted at the rear. Despite its modest power, the car offered surprising practicality and affordability, quickly gaining popularity and spawning numerous Abarth-tuned variants. The F model introduced front-hinged doors for the first time.
cars.hero: Small, versatile and inexpensive, this minimalist car could also be raced.

cars.description: The FIAT Panda is a front-wheel-drive hatchback introduced in 1980, born amid the compact-car boom that followed the oil crises. Its design was penned by the master stylist Giorgetto Giugiaro. To keep costs low, the body was crafted with straight lines and flat panels, achieving a look that was both practical and modern. At launch, buyers could choose between an air-cooled 652 cc 2-cylinder engine or a water-cooled 903 cc 4-cylinder unit. The model featured in Gran Turismo is the former.
cars.hero: This jewel of a compact car is the one designer Giugiaro called his greatest work.

cars.description: Introduced in 1992, the Escort RS Cosworth was a homologation model built to support Ford’s campaign in the WRC. It inherited the 2.0-liter twin-cam engine from the Sierra, producing 223.9 HP, and featured a 4-wheel-drive system that delivered exceptional rally performance. The car proved its capability with a 1-2 finish at the Rally de Portugal, followed by back-to-back victories in the Tour de Corse and Acropolis Rally, firmly reestablishing Ford as a force in the world of rallying.
cars.hero: A WRC homologation special with a unique double-decker wing design.

cars.description: The F-Series is Ford’s line of full-size pickup trucks, introduced in 1948. Over the decades, it became a staple of American roads and has held the title of the best-selling vehicle in the U.S. for more than 30 years. The F-150 SVT Raptor, developed by Ford’s Special Vehicle Team (SVT), was a purpose-built off-road variant of the F-150, using the same 4-wheel-drive system as its base model, for high-speed desert racing.
cars.hero: With 411.2 HP on tap, this was one of the most potent pickup trucks ever created, thanks to Ford's Special Vehicle Team.

cars.description: A Gran Turismo Original, Ford’s Focus global hatchback has been reimagined to meet the demands of Gr.B regulations. To accommodate the changes, air intakes have been added just ahead of the rear fenders, channeling airflow to a rear-mounted radiator. Relocating the radiator to the trunk improved weight distribution, making it one of the most easy-to-drive machines in the Gr.B category.
cars.hero: The chassis performance of the late third-generation model shines in this rally special.

cars.description: Introduced in 2018, the fourth-generation Ford Focus included a high-performance RS variant in its lineup. This iteration marked the first time the RS featured 4-wheel drive, complete with adjustable torque distribution for enhanced handling. New selectable drive modes, such as "Track" and "Drift," were introduced, complementing an improved chassis and damping system. At its core was a 2.3-liter inline-4 EcoBoost engine producing 345.2 HP. With a zero–62.1 mph time of 4.7 seconds and a top speed of 165.3 mph, the car delivered remarkable performance in a compact package.
cars.hero: The RS model of the third-generation Ford Focus was the first to get 4-wheel drive.

cars.description: Since its debut in 1998, the Focus ST—the performance model in the Focus lineup—has remained a favorite among driving enthusiasts. The “ST” designation stands for “Sports Technology." In its third generation, the ST adopted a smaller engine than its predecessor, yet output was increased by 24.7 HP, bringing the total to 246.5 HP. Aimed squarely at purists, it retained a 6-speed manual transmission, a rare offering in a market increasingly dominated by two-pedal alternatives.
cars.hero: Ford's Sport Technology was on full display in this late-model, compact performance car.

cars.description: Built to commemorate Ford’s 100th anniversary, the Ford GT drew both its silhouette and spirit from the iconic GT40—a legend born from its sweep of the top three positions at the 1966 24 Hours of Le Mans, and its unprecedented four-year winning streak that followed through 1969. With a 0–60 mph time of just 3.3 seconds and a top speed of 205.1 mph, the GT delivered performance worthy of its heritage. A total of 4,038 units were produced over a three-year span, concluding in 2006.
cars.hero: The final-year model of this potent supercar came right after the company's 100th anniversary.

cars.description: Between 2005 and 2006, Ford produced the GT, a modern homage to the legendary GT40. A decade later, in 2015, a second-generation model was unveiled. While retaining the unmistakable lineage of the GT40, it introduced an aggressively aerodynamic form and cutting-edge engineering. Built around a carbon-fiber monocoque with aluminum subframes, it was significantly lighter and delivered a top speed of 216.2 mph.
cars.hero: The second-generation Ford GT came complete with reengineered aerodynamics.

cars.description: This LM-spec machine represented a Le Mans–style reinterpretation of the Ford GT—an evolution of the 1960s GT40 legacy, infused with modern technology. Under the rear deck sat a supercharged 5.4-liter DOHC V-8 producing 591.7 HP. It also featured a double wishbone suspension and a race-ready 6-speed gearbox.
cars.hero: Gran Turismo commemorates the return of the legendary Le Mans-winning machine by offering its own interpretation.
cars.model: Ford GT LM Race Car Spec II
cars.name_long: Ford GT LM Race Car Spec II

cars.description: This LM-spec race car took the 2004 Ford GT and reengineered it for the rigors of Le Mans competition. Power output was raised from the street version’s 550.3 HP to 591.7 HP, while the body—faithful in size and shape to the production GT—was reconstructed entirely in carbon fiber, bringing curb weight down to just 2535 lbs.
cars.hero: Gran Turismo commemorates the return of the legendary Le Mans-winning machine by offering its own interpretation.
cars.model: Ford GT LM Spec II Test Car
cars.name_long: Ford GT LM Spec II Test Car

cars.description: Unveiled in 2015, the second-generation Ford GT focused on aerodynamics and speed, with a compact twin-turbo V-6 engine delivering zero–to -62.1 mph in 3.0 seconds and a top speed of 216.2 mph. In racing, Chip Ganassi Racing represented the United States in both the FIA World Endurance Championship and IMSA starting in 2016.
cars.hero: This race car claimed numerous World Endurance Championship titles.

cars.description: The car’s spirit is deeply rooted in American custom car and hot rod culture, a tradition that traces back to the 1930s. Model T and Model B Fords were often boldly modified, with exterior customizations and engine swaps for more powerful units. The V-3883, displayed in the Henry Ford Museum, features a Chrysler 331 Hemi engine producing 177.5 HP. A relatively simple yet striking example, its exposed engine cover serves as a key visual accent, capturing the essence of early American hot rod craftsmanship.
cars.hero: This "High Boy"-style hot rod was displayed at the Henry Ford Museum.

cars.description: In a bold move to leave its mark on the racing world, Ford partnered with Lola Cars to develop the Mark I, which was completed in 1964. Based on the Lola-designed Mk6, the car was introduced as the Ford GT. The name "GT40" was coined by a reporter, amazed by the car’s height—just 40 inches from the ground. At the 1966 24 Hours of Le Mans, the improved Mark II version achieved a legendary 1-2-3 finish.
cars.hero: This historic machine achieved a much-desired Le Mans victory with an incredible 1-2-3 finish.

cars.description: Following this triumph, Ford responded to updated FIA regulations by developing the Mark IV—a new test car with a highly aerodynamic body. This redesign pushed the top speed to 215.6 mph and significantly improved high-speed stability, crucial to its success in the 1967 Le Mans. There, the Mark IV outpaced its rival by five laps, securing a second consecutive victory for Ford at the famed endurance race.
cars.hero: This race car represented Ford's last effort to challenge for the 24 Hours of Le Mans title.

cars.description: This enhanced variant was exclusively offered on the 1969 and 1970 model years of Ford’s original Mustang. Built for NASCAR homologation, this Mustang housed the largest engine ever fitted to the model—a 7.0-liter V-8 known as the 429. Easily identified by its prominent hood scoop, it is often hailed as the most powerful Mustang in the model’s storied history.
cars.hero: This special high-performance Mustang was produced for only two years.

cars.description: The Mustang Gr.3 is a Gran Turismo Original creation, transforming Ford’s legendary Mustang coupe into a machine built to meet Gr.3 race regulations. Its fenders have been dramatically widened to accommodate broader tires, while large rear air outlets were integrated to efficiently channel airflow. This modern muscle car excels through the stability offered by its long wheelbase and boasts an exceptional top speed that’s hard to match.
cars.hero: The sixth-generation Mustang marked the model’s 50th anniversary and was sold in 120 countries around the world.

cars.description: This particular version serves as a homologation model of the Mustang Gr.3—a Gran Turismo Original that reimagines Ford’s legendary coupe to comply with Gr.3 racing regulations. With its roots in motorsport, the car’s performance has been finely tuned, placing particular emphasis on cornering prowess. A true all-rounder, it excels equally in circuit time attacks and controlled drifting alike.
cars.hero: The sixth-generation Mustang marked the model’s 50th anniversary and was sold in 120 countries around the world.

cars.description: The Mustang Gr.4 is a Gran Turismo Original model that reimagines Ford’s iconic Mustang coupe to comply with Gr.4 race regulations. Built upon the inherently stable platform of the production model, this touring car is an ideal choice for newcomers. Visually, it commands attention with the timeless appeal of classic Ford racing stripes adorning its exterior.
cars.hero: The 50th Anniversary sixth-generation Ford Mustang GT goes international.

cars.description: The Mustang Gr.B was a Gran Turismo Original creation, reimagining Ford’s legendary Mustang coupe to comply with Gr.B rally regulations. Its livery draws inspiration from the factory colors of the Ford GT race program. Although it may have seemed an unlikely candidate at first glance, the car echoes Ford’s rich rallying heritage, embodied by icons like the Escort and RS200, making the concept feel surprisingly authentic.
cars.hero: The 50th Anniversary sixth-generation Ford Mustang GT goes international.

cars.description: In 2014, marking the 50th anniversary of the Mustang’s debut and amid unprecedented global demand, Ford unveiled the sixth-generation model after an intensive development effort. This new iteration featured more aggressive styling and introduced 4-wheel independent suspension for the first time in the car’s lineage. Among many variants in the lineup, it is the Mustang GT that captures the hearts of true enthusiasts, thanks to its iconic V-8 powerplant.
cars.hero: The 50th Anniversary sixth-generation Ford Mustang GT goes international.

cars.description: Following its debut in 1964, the original Ford Mustang underwent a transformation in 1969, adopting a larger and more muscular body design. Among the updated lineup, the Mach 1, distinguished by its bold SportsRoof fastback, stood out for its aggressive appearance. Its styling left a lasting impression, influencing sports car design across the globe for years to come.
cars.hero: With more muscle than others in its class, this pony car set a new standard for aggressiveness.

cars.description: The original GT350R was developed for race competition in 1965, based on the original Mustang. The 2016 Shelby GT350R was similarly based on the seventh generation Mustang, with the engine tuned to 525.6 HP. The chassis components supporting the engine performance were also upgraded, resulting in a car that was fit to go to the circuit straight from the factory.
cars.hero: This high-performance model of the seventh-generation Mustang takes its name from a legend.

cars.description: The Sierra RS Cosworth was created in 1995 by the masters at Cosworth. Originally a family car, the Sierra’s 2L inline-4 engine was fully tuned, adding a DOHC head and turbocharger, along with other chassis upgrades. The Sierra RS500 Cosworth was introduced a year later. Between 1988 and 1990, it competed in Group A category races around the world, winning several championship titles.
cars.hero: A Cosworth tuned masterpiece that dominated touring car racing.

cars.description: Introduced in 2017, the Genesis G70 sports sedan marked the brand’s entry-level offering. It came with three powertrain options: a 3.3-liter twin-turbo V-6 producing 364.9 HP, a turbocharged 2.0-liter gasoline, and a 2.2-liter turbodiesel. A major facelift followed in 2020, incorporating design cues from Genesis’ flagship models. In 2021, a shooting brake variant—offered exclusively in Europe—further elevated the G70’s appeal.
cars.hero: An AWD Genesis sports sedan powered by a potent twin-turbo V-6.

cars.description: As the entry point to the Genesis lineup, the G70 plays a key role in introducing drivers to the brand’s appeal. Its design was refreshed in 2020 with styling cues from flagship models, and in 2021, a sleek shooting brake variant was launched exclusively for the European market. The Genesis G70 GR4 is a Gran Turismo-spec machine, finely tuned for Gr.4 competition.
cars.hero: An AWD Genesis sports sedan powered by a potent twin-turbo V-6.

cars.description: In April 2021, Genesis revealed its vision for the future of grand touring with the Genesis X Concept. Showcasing the brand’s "Athletic Elegance" design language, it featured the signature crest grille and clean, straight body lines. The Genesis X GR3 carries this design philosophy into the world of motorsports. This innovative Gr.3 machine embodies the fusion of luxury and racing prowess.
cars.hero: A Gr.3 machine that combines luxury with competition performance.

cars.description: The Genesis X Gran Berlinetta Vision Gran Turismo Concept embodies the pinnacle of the brand’s design philosophy. It features Genesis’ signature anti-wedge profile, introducing fresh design ideas for future sports models. Powered by the Lambda II V-6 with electric assist, it produces 1,071 hp (1071 HP). It represents a perfect balance of sculpted beauty and raw performance.
cars.hero: A sports coupe that embodies the athletic elegance sought by Genesis.
cars.model: Genesis X Gran Berlinetta VGT Concept
cars.name_long: Genesis X Gran Berlinetta Vision Gran Turismo Concept

cars.description: The Genesis X Gran Racer Vision Gran Turismo Concept is the ultimate expression of Genesis’ "Athletic Elegance." This Racer version dramatically increases downforce to enhance lap times. Its hybrid powertrain paired a V-6 engine with electric assists to deliver a staggering 1518.7 HP and 1,015 ft-lb (1014.8 ft-lb) of torque.
cars.hero: The racing version of the Gran Berlinetta adorned with aerodynamic parts.
cars.model: Genesis X Gran Racer VGT Concept
cars.name_long: Genesis X Gran Racer Vision Gran Turismo Concept

cars.description: The Gran Turismo F1500T-A was a modern tribute to the mid-1980s era of Formula 1, widely regarded as the golden age of F1 design. Its carbon-fiber chassis measured 166.7 inches in length, 84.5 inches in width, with a wheelbase of 107.0 inches. Power came from a turbocharged 1.5-liter V-6, a hallmark of 1980s F1, producing a staggering 986.2 HP at 11,000 rpm.
cars.hero: This original formula car adopted the spirit and performance of the mid-1980s Formula 1 race cars.

cars.description: The F3500-A, a Gran Turismo original, was born from a deep admiration for early 1990s Formula 1 machines. It was built around a carbon-fiber chassis and equipped with pushrod suspension. Its naturally-aspirated 3.5-liter V-12 screamed to 15,000 rpm and was paired with a 6-speed semiautomatic transmission. Formula cars continue to evolve. The F3500-A stands as a benchmark—an idealized representation of just how far performance and design had advanced during that era.
cars.hero: An original formula car created in the image of classic F1 cars.

cars.description: The F3500-A was conceived as a tribute to the early 1990s Formula 1 race cars, and the F3500-B proudly carries that legacy forward. Its most significant evolution lies in the powertrain. While the F3500-A was powered by a V-12, the F3500-B adopts a compact, lightweight V-8. Although smaller in displacement, this engine revs to an astonishing 13,800 rpm, generating more than 700.2 HP in the process. The F3500-B also offers three distinct front wing configurations for its high-nose layout.
cars.hero: Here's a V-8 version of the GT original formula car.

cars.description: While racing karts are typically viewed as the gateway to motorsports, the Shifter Kart is more akin to a sub-formula race car. Equipped with a 125 cc water-cooled two-stroke engine mated to a 6-speed gearbox and featuring front-only braking, it is capable of reaching speeds up to 124.3 mph. This is a racing machine that hones the skills of race drivers.
cars.hero: With its tremendous performance and 6-speed gearbox, this kart proves fast enough for full-size tracks.

cars.description: The X2014 Series was the result of a collaborative “fan car” project between Red Bull Racing and Gran Turismo. The entry-level X2014 Junior model combined a compact body with a similarly compact engine producing approximately 246.5 HP, making it the ideal platform for learning the fundamentals of formula driving.
cars.hero: A beginner level machine for learning the basics of formula cars.
cars.name_long: Gran Turismo Red Bull X2014 Junior

cars.description: The X2014 Series was the result of a collaborative “fan car” project between Red Bull Racing and Gran Turismo. The mid-tier X2014 Standard followed as a more advanced model, developed as a conventional Venturi car. Its design minimized aerodynamic drag through front and rear wheel covers and a glass canopy, while simultaneously increasing downforce.
cars.hero: A traditional venturi car with the axial flow fan and skirts removed from the X2014.
cars.name_long: Gran Turismo Red Bull X2014 Standard

cars.description: The X2019 Competition was developed at the inception of the Gran Turismo Championship, with the goal of creating a race car that was as thrilling to watch as it was to drive. Based on the X2014 Standard, it featured revised design elements, including new front wheel styling, a reworked rear body structure, and reshaped rear wheel covers. Also, the powertrain was updated from a turbocharged 2.0-liter engine to a naturally-aspirated 3.0-liter unit, and the throttle system was replaced with a more conventional mechanical setup.
cars.hero: This is an evolution of the X2014 created for the FIA Gran Turismo Championships.
cars.name_long: Gran Turismo Red Bull X2019 Competition

cars.description: This car was the winner of the GT Award at SEMA 2015. Built by actor Sung Kang, it started with a 1973 Nissan 240Z as its foundation. It was powered by an RB26DETT engine sourced from a GT-R, which was converted to natural aspiration and tuned to produce 216 HP. The car’s aggressive styling was enhanced with wide over-fenders and front and rear spoilers crafted by Rocket Bunny.
cars.hero: This "poisonous" 240Z, which won the 2015 GT Award, packed a naturally-aspirated RB26 engine.

cars.description: This striking machine was the winner of the 2017 Gran Turismo Award. Based on a 1992 EG Honda Civic, it features a PANDEM wide-body kit and a carbon-fiber hood inspired by a design from J's Racing. The interior has been fully stripped to reduce weight, and the original engine has been replaced with a K24 inline-4. This car stood as a striking symbol of the JDM (Japanese Domestic Market) scene.
cars.hero: A time attack Civic customized in the classic JDM style.

cars.description: The 1971 Ford Maverick, winner of the 2018 SEMA “Best of Show,” was crafted by Greening Auto Company into a striking custom build. Its ride height was dropped to the limit for maximum visual impact. The 7.0-liter Windsor V-8 was equipped with twin turbochargers to generate 1199.2 HP, yet it also offered flexibility—its engine control logic could be adjusted for a more relaxed, street-friendly cruise.
cars.hero: A vicious hot rod with 1200HP and a nostalgic body

cars.description: The "Honda Project 2&4 powered by RC213V" was the result of a collaboration between Honda’s design team and Gran Turismo. It combined the 212 HP engine from the Honda RC213V-S with an ultra-lightweight 893 lbs body, creating a unique form of mobility that offered the open-air freedom and agility of a motorcycle, combined with the handling precision and lateral G-forces of a 4-wheeled vehicle.
cars.hero: A new species with the openness of a motorcycle and the handling of an automobile.

cars.description: Launched in 1991, the Honda Beat helped spark the boom in lightweight two-seat sports cars. Tipping the scales at just 1675 lbs, it also delivered near-perfect balance with a 43:57 front-to-rear weight ratio. Its engine, infused with F1-derived technology and paired with a short-stroke transmission, delivered a driving experience like no other. And you didn’t need mountain roads to enjoy it—the Beat brought pure sports car fun to your everyday drive.
cars.hero: This wonderful kei sports car offered style and driving excitement never before seen in Japan.

cars.description: In 1987, Honda introduced the all-new fourth-generation Civic. It was known as the Grand Civic, with the model code EF. Its most significant advancement was a complete platform overhaul, bringing double wishbone suspension to all four corners. The sporty Si model and the more luxurious Si Extra both featured the 1.6-liter DOHC ZC inline-4 engine. These models also found success on the track, competing in the Japan Touring Car Championship and securing championship titles.
cars.hero: A dominating force on the touring car circuit, this fourth-generation Civic features the famous ZC engine.

cars.description: This Civic Si Group A version was modeled after the MUGEN MOTUL CIVIC, a Group A race car based on the third-generation Si, Honda's first production car in 14 years to feature a DOHC engine. In Division 1 of the All-Japan Touring Car Championship, for cars with engine displacements from 1001 cc to 1600 cc, it was unstoppable, winning its class in all six rounds and securing the 1987 Manufacturers' title for Honda.
cars.hero: An undefeated race machine that dominated its class in 1987.
cars.name_long: Honda Civic Si Group A version '87

cars.description: The Civic is Honda’s longest-running model line. The fifth-generation EG Civic, introduced in September 1991, was promoted as the “sports Civic.” At the top of the range sat the SiR grade, equipped with a 1.6-liter DOHC VTEC engine. Building on the success of the previous SiR, which had already achieved the benchmark of 100 horsepower per liter, this model delivered an additional 9.9 HP, bringing total output to 167.7 HP.
cars.hero: The top-of-the-line fifth-generation Civic balances speed with comfort.

cars.description: First introduced in 1972, the Civic is Honda’s longest-running model. In 1997, the first Civic Type R made its debut, based on the sixth-generation Civic. At its heart was the B16B—a 1.6-liter naturally-aspirated inline-4 DOHC engine that delivered an impressive 182.4 HP. True to the Type R philosophy, the car featured extensive weight reduction and upgraded suspension components. The result was a car that found success across the spectrum of motorsport, from professional racing series to grassroots competition.
cars.hero: This car represented the first Type R model that eventually dominated circuits around the world.

cars.description: In Honda’s lineup, the "Type R" designation signified production models specifically tuned for high performance. The Civic Type R first appeared in August 1997. Based on the sixth-generation EK Civic, it was powered by the B16B 1.6-liter inline-4 DOHC 16-valve engine. Thanks to Honda’s VTEC system, it produced 182.4 HP at 8200 rpm without any forced induction. The model quickly earned a reputation in motorsports, becoming a favorite among amateur racers.
cars.hero: This car represented the first Type R model that eventually dominated circuits around the world.

cars.description: First introduced in 1972, the Civic is Honda’s longest-running model. In 1997, the first Civic Type R made its debut, based on the sixth-generation Civic. At its heart was the B16B—a 1.6-liter naturally-aspirated inline-4 DOHC engine that delivered an impressive 182.4 HP. This version is an original Gran Turismo-tuned model based on the 1997 Civic Type R (EK).
cars.hero: The first Type R model tuned by Gran Turismo.
cars.name_long: Honda Civic Type R (EK) Touring Car

cars.description: The Civic Type R has thrilled driving enthusiasts worldwide since its debut in 1997. A new model was developed on the ninth-generation European-market 5-door hatchback, undergoing extensive wind tunnel and circuit testing in the pursuit of pure performance. It set a benchmark at the Nürburgring Nordschleife with a lap time of 7 minutes and 50.63 seconds, establishing a new record for front-wheel-drive production cars.
cars.hero: One of the world's most beloved pocket rockets comes back with a vengeance.

cars.description: The sixth-generation Honda Civic Type R was unveiled in September 2022. It was based on the FL 5-door hatchback variant of the 11th-generation Civic. Powering the car was a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 K20C engine, delivering 325.4 HP and 309.6 ft-lb of torque, surpassing the previous generation in both output and response. Updates to the 4-wheel independent active damper system further enhanced chassis performance, sharpening the car’s dynamic capability on both road and track.
cars.hero: Driving feel comes first. The legendary R badge returns for the 11th generation Civic.

cars.description: The fifth-generation Civic Type R made its debut in 2017. While previous models focused on enhancing the base Civic’s performance, the fifth-generation Type R was developed in parallel with the standard model from the ground up. In 2020, the lineup was further refined with the introduction of the Limited Edition model. Weight was reduced by 44 lbs through the removal of soundproofing materials and the adoption of specially forged wheels. Subtle suspension tweaks were also made to sharpen handling. With only 1,000 units produced worldwide, the Limited Edition sold out almost immediately.
cars.hero: What will no doubt be a collector car someday, the limited-edition Civic Type R sold out in minutes.
cars.name_long: Honda Civic Type R Limited Edition (FK8) '20

cars.description: In the 1990s, Honda introduced the “Creative Mover” category, launching the original CR-V in 1995 as part of that vision. By 2021, the fifth-generation CR-V had evolved significantly, with this model becoming the first in the series to feature a hybrid powertrain. A 4-wheel-drive option remained popular, offering added versatility. Its larger body improved interior space and expanded cargo capacity to over 1,100 liters. A 3-row, 7-seat configuration further enhanced practicality. Equipped with a wide range of safety features and advanced driver assistance systems, it proved to be an ideal vehicle for daily use.
cars.hero: The fifth-generation model of this popular SUV is the first to feature a hybrid system.

cars.description: The original Fit Hybrid debuted in 2010, drawing considerable attention as the first hybrid offering in the B-segment. In 2013, the second-generation Fit Hybrid arrived, built upon the third-generation Fit platform. This updated model featured the Sport Hybrid i-DCD system, paired with a 1.5-liter i-VTEC engine to deliver a combined 137.1 HP. In Japan’s JC08 fuel efficiency cycle, it achieved an impressive rating of 85.7 MPG.
cars.hero: The third-generation hybrid Fit utilized i-DCD to maximize energy efficiency.

cars.description: The Honda Sports Vision Gran Turismo is a two-seater coupe born from a collaboration between Honda’s design team and Gran Turismo. It embodies Honda’s "Human Centered Design" philosophy, featuring a driver-focused package that prioritized engagement and usability. With bold, athletic proportions, the car delivers the striking presence and excitement expected of a true sports car.
cars.hero: This lightweight mid-engine sports car embodied Honda's "Power of Dreams" philosophy.

cars.description: This high-performance version of the Integra was introduced in 1995. Its B18C engine, derived from the Si model, was enhanced with high-compression pistons, reinforced connecting rods, and dual valve springs, all assembled by hand for maximum precision. The body saw increased rigidity alongside weight reduction, while the suspension was completely reworked to deliver sharp, balanced handling with virtually no understeer. It earned the nickname “the road-going race car.”
cars.hero: The first Type R model of the Integra, this car was built to be the ultimate front-wheel drive sports car.

cars.description: This car introduced the concept of the Type R, a road-going race car. At its heart was the 1.8-liter VTEC B18C engine, hand-built with a high-compression head and carefully matched connecting rods to produce 197.2 HP. While performance parts like the helical LSD added weight, it was offset by stripping out comfort features, resulting in pure speed.
cars.hero: This third-gen Integra Type R received more power and hand-crafted tuning.

cars.description: Honda’s N-ONE was a retro-inspired kei-car that paid homage to the company's first entry into the segment, the classic N360. The second-generation model retained the charming silhouette of the original, but rode on a completely new chassis that brought modern refinement to its compact dimensions. Among the highlights of the lineup was the RS trim, a sporty variant that borrowed close-ratio gearing from the S660 sports car. It featured reinforced synchronizers for second and third gear, and a heavy-duty clutch to handle spirited driving. While the RS badge had been offered on the first-gen N-ONE, the new RS stood out as the first kei-car to pair a turbocharged, front-wheel-drive layout with a 6-speed manual transmission — a groundbreaking move in the world of Japan’s smallest cars.
cars.hero: This performance-focused model is a first kei-car with front-wheel drive, a turbocharged engine and a 6-speed manual transmission.

cars.description: Making its official debut 25 years after the original, the second-generation NSX emerged as a true supercar, equipped with an advanced electric all-wheel-drive system called the Sports Hybrid SH-AWD, which employed independent electric motors on the front wheels. By enhancing both acceleration and deceleration, it enabled torque vectoring that provided exceptional stability through corners across the entire speed range.
cars.hero: Acura's popular exotic sports car returns after a 10-year hiatus.

cars.description: The NSX CONCEPT-GT was a purpose-built racing machine developed by Honda, based on the 2012 next-generation NSX concept, to compete in the GT500 class of the Super GT series. At its debut, the car featured a hybrid powertrain, however, by the 2016 season, the hybrid system was removed due to supply challenges from the battery manufacturer. It concluded the season with a 12th-place finish overall.
cars.hero: This race machine claimed the Super GT championship in 2016 equipped with a conventional gasoline engine.

cars.description: A Gran Turismo Original, Honda’s flagship NSX sports car has been reengineered to comply with Gr.3 racing regulations. It features a range of aerodynamic enhancements, including a large front splitter with precision cutouts to manage airflow, and a swan-neck rear wing.
cars.hero: Acura's popular exotic sports car returns after a 10-year hiatus.

cars.description: A Gran Turismo Original, Honda’s flagship NSX sports car has been adapted to meet Gr.4 regulations. This design prioritizes preserving the character of the base car, adding only a subtle front splitter, compact canards, and a rear wing. To enhance structural rigidity, a rear bulkhead has been added, accompanied by a rear camera.
cars.hero: This second-generation NSX with SH-AWD was modified for Gr.4 competition.

cars.description: A Gran Turismo Original, Honda’s flagship NSX has been reimagined to conform to Gr.B rally regulations. While sporting a rugged rally-cross exterior, it retains the NSX’s signature mid-engine layout, now paired with a 4-wheel-drive system. The original rear-biased weight distribution has been preserved, promising thrilling tail-out dynamics on loose surfaces.
cars.hero: The NSX was revived with SH-AWD 25 years after the debut of the original model.

cars.description: The 2000 All Japan Grand Touring Championship (JGTC) GT500 class saw fierce competition among Japan’s top three automakers: Honda, Toyota, and Nissan. That year, five teams fielded the NSX. They included the Castrol MUGEN NSX and Takata Dome NSX, running as official factory entries. While the Takata Dome NSX demonstrated remarkable potential, it was the Castrol MUGEN NSX, featured here, that claimed the championship. Its success came through strategic management of the weight handicaps, showcasing speed and discipline over the course of the season.
cars.hero: A new design with a lower center of gravity was the key to victory for this JGTC champion.

cars.description: This is a version of the NSX that competed in the 2008 Super GT championship. Despite facing disadvantages that season—including running with the previous year’s chassis, weight handicaps, and a restricted air intake—the car remained competitive thanks to significant improvements in both engine performance and aerodynamics. In Round 8 at Autopolis, the EPSON NSX secured a 2nd-place finish.
cars.hero: The special race NSX brings to mind the bold driving styles of racers Loic Duval and Katsuyuki Hiranaka.

cars.description: The second-wave NSX Type R made its debut in 2002. In addition to the original Type R’s weight-saving measures and increased rigidity, this model underwent a full aerodynamic redesign, generating remarkable levels of downforce rarely seen in a road car. Carbon fiber was employed extensively, including for key components such as the hood and rear wing. During a time attack at the Nürburgring Nordschleife, the car shattered expectations by breaking the eight-minute barrier, a feat once thought unattainable for a road car.
cars.hero: Thanks to advancements in aerodynamics, the 2nd-gen NSX had more downforce than the original.

cars.description: A high-performance variant of the NSX was introduced in November 1992. Weight was reduced by 265 lbs through the elimination of luxury amenities and the use of lighter functional components. Each engine was carefully balanced to deliver a refined and exhilarating experience at high rpm. It remains a legendary model, one whose significance in the evolution of the NSX cannot be overstated.
cars.hero: The first of the Honda Type R series, only 500 cars of this rare model were produced.

cars.description: In 1965, this legendary machine delivered Honda its first-ever F1 victory. Building upon the foundation of the RA271—Honda’s first F1 challenger—this car achieved greater performance through weight reduction across its components, the adoption of outboard rear suspension, and refined tuning of its 1.5-liter V-12. Although early in the season it grappled with stability issues, significant improvements were introduced midway through the campaign. These efforts culminated in a hard-fought and celebrated triumph at Round 10, the Mexican Grand Prix.
cars.hero: The F1 machine that scored Honda its first F1 victory.

cars.description: Honda's beloved 'S' series of the 1960s made a return in 1999. Every element of the S2000 was engineered from the ground up to deliver pure, focused driving performance. True to its name, it was powered by a 2.0-liter DOHC inline-4 engine. Its 6-speed manual transmission was a purpose-built unit, incorporating a secondary reduction gear to optimize shift feel while minimizing weight. Details like these offered a clear window into the passion and precision that defined the S2000's development.
cars.hero: The FR open top sports car debuted for the 50th anniversary of Honda.

cars.description: The S660 marked Honda’s return to the convertible ultralight kei-sports-car segment 19 years after the end of production of the Beat in 1996. Its all-new body design delivered exceptional rigidity while maintaining a featherweight curb mass in the low 1764 lbs range. Adding to its dynamic prowess, the S660 featured a torque vectoring system that enabled cornering performance previously unimaginable for a kei-car, offering neutral, engaging handling.
cars.hero: The spiritual successor to the Beat was this small-yet-unadulterated mid-engine kei sports car.

cars.description: Honda’s lineage of sports cars began in 1963 with the ultra-compact, two-seat S500. It was followed by the S600, which delivered more power through a larger engine, and then by the S800, which featured 4-wheel independent suspension. Equipped with a more robust engine than the S600 and a short-throw shift lever positioned within easy reach of its low-slung seats, the S800 earned international praise.
cars.hero: With a larger displacement than its predecessor, this car represented the pinnacle of the "S" line.

cars.description: The sixth-generation Step WGN minivan featured a low floor and large sliding doors, creating an extremely practical package that earned widespread support from families. Of the many versions in the lineup, the Spada Premium Line was the most luxurious, featuring exclusive platinum-style chrome trim, a high-quality dark-toned interior and a 7-seat layout with second-row captain's chairs for exceptional comfort.
cars.hero: This upper-grade version of the sixth-generation Step WGN, with improvements in driving performance, space and refinement.
cars.name_long: Honda Step WGN Spada Premium Line '23

cars.description: Introduced as the high-performance model of the seventh-generation ELANTRA, the ELANTRA N was developed to embody the N brand philosophy of “making cornering fun.” Powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter engine producing 276.1 HP and 289.3 ft-lb of torque, it accelerated from 0-62.1 mph in just 5.3 seconds, despite its front-wheel-drive layout. It was offered with either a 6-speed manual transmission or an 8-speed DCT. Its running gear featured electronically controlled dampers and an eLSD, complemented by a robust braking system.
cars.hero: This track-ready Elantra is brought to you by the letter "N."

cars.description: The Hyundai ELANTRA N TC was a special model built for racing. Based on the ELANTRA N, which could accelerate from 0–62.1 mph in just 5.3 seconds despite using a front-wheel-drive layout, the TC model was specially outfitted according to touring-car race regulations. The wide body was equipped with a carbon-fiber splitter and a large rear wing to greatly improve high-speed cornering stability. This model was also fitted with a 6-speed sequential gearbox, with the braking and cooling parts upgraded to endurance-racing standards.
cars.hero: This track-oriented Elantra was meticulously crafted to achieve victory.

cars.description: This sports coupe used the same platform as the Genesis luxury sedan. It was 13.6 inches shorter overall, with a wheelbase 4.5 inches shorter. Combined with a front-engine/rear-wheel-drive layout and 4-wheel independent suspension, the car possessed sharp handling dynamics. In 2012, the model received updates that increased engine output. With its 3.8-liter V-6 producing around 345.2 HP, it achieved performance approaching supercar territory.
cars.hero: Circuit-developed components characterized this high-performance sports car.

cars.description: Hyundai’s rear-wheel-drive Genesis sports car has been modified to meet Gr.3 regulations for this Gran Turismo Original. With a wheelbase exceeding 110.2 inches, it delivers excellent stability and strong downforce thanks to its expansive floor surface. The naturally-aspirated V-6 produces more than 493.1 HP, offering impressive performance without forced induction. It was a well-balanced machine, capable of excelling through both corners and straights.
cars.hero: Circuit-developed components characterized this high-performance sports car.

cars.description: Hyundai’s rear-wheel-drive Genesis sports car has been adapted to meet Gr.4 regulations for this Gran Turismo Original. Although it appears externally as a touring car, features like its paddle-shift transmission brought it closer in spirit to a Gr.3 machine. In the real world, this car earned a strong reputation in the drifting scene, and this Gr.4 version proves just as capable for racing as it was for sliding sideways.
cars.hero: Circuit-developed components characterized this high-performance sports car.

cars.description: Hyundai’s rear-wheel-drive Genesis sports car has been reengineered to meet Gr.B regulations for this Gran Turismo Original. A 4-wheel-drive conversion has been added, along with design elements inspired by modern rally machines. The front fenders feature smooth, organic curves to maximize downforce, while the wide track, measuring more than 80.7 inches, enhanced maneuverability, complementing the car’s long wheelbase.
cars.hero: Circuit-developed components characterized this high-performance sports car.

cars.description: Created to commemorate Hyundai’s 50th anniversary, this model also embodied the spirit and ambition of the company's high-performance "N" division. It was powered by hydrogen fuel cells paired with supercapacitors that stored energy recovered through regenerative braking, delivering a combined output of 650 kW (871.8 HP) via electric motors at each wheel. Thanks to compact, lightweight fuel-cell stacks and a CFRP monocoque chassis, the car tipped the scales at just 2143 lbs.
cars.hero: An extreme monster machine that embodies the passion and future of Hyundai's "N".

cars.description: Originally created through a collaboration between Hyundai and Gran Turismo, the N 2025 Vision Gran Turismo has been reworked to meet Gr.1 regulations in this original model. In accordance with Gr.1 rules, the variable rear wing is fixed in place. The 4-wheel-drive system remains unchanged, giving the car exceptional grip and allowing it to handle as if it were glued to the tarmac.
cars.hero: This extreme car embodies the passion and future of Hyundai's "N" brand.

cars.description: This performance model was introduced two years after the original launch of the IONIQ 5. It featured a 4-wheel-drive system powered by electric motors on the front and rear axles, allowing for freely adjustable torque distribution. When set to a rear-wheel bias, the system enabled the over two-ton SUV to be drifted with ease. In an effort to preserve the excitement of traditional combustion-engine cars, this unique electric SUV also offered a simulated 8-speed dual-clutch transmission and synthetic exhaust sounds.
cars.hero: A fearsome driving machine that challenges the preconceptions of BEVs.

cars.description: This was the second high-performance EV from Hyundai N. Equipped with a power unit with 770 Nm of torque and 641 HP of total system output, in a body tuned for aerodynamic performance, it accelerates from zero to 62.1 mph in just 3.2 seconds. Features such as N Active Sound+ and N e-Shift, which gave the feeling of gear shifts in an EV, showed Hyundai N’s dedication to preserving the fun of driving.
cars.hero: A new paradigm for high-performance EV.

cars.description: The INFINITI CONCEPT Vision Gran Turismo was developed by the Infiniti premium brand under the guiding philosophy of “designing a pure INFINITI GT car.” The design team set out to create a full-fledged race machine, while also crafting a seductive and distinctive race design language.
cars.hero: High performance made possible with a V8 engine and electrical motor. A GT machine packed with the motorsport passion of Asia.

cars.description: This Vision Gran Turismo came from a renowned Italian design house. Its name was derived from the Latin word xenium, meaning “gift for the guest.” Its design encases both driver and engine in layered carbon fiber and aluminum, resulting in a distinctive wrapped appearance. A V-10 engine has been mounted behind the cockpit, while two electric motors powered the front wheels. To adapt to various terrain conditions, the chassis can be adjusted into four different configurations.
cars.hero: A high-performance luxury car prepared as a "beautifully wrapped gift."
cars.name_long: Italdesign EXENEO Vision Gran Turismo Off-road Mode

cars.description: This Vision Gran Turismo came from a renowned Italian design house. Its name was derived from the Latin word xenium, meaning “gift for the guest.” Its design encases both driver and engine in layered carbon fiber and aluminum, resulting in a distinctive wrapped appearance. A V-10 engine has been mounted behind the cockpit, while two electric motors powered the front wheels. To adapt to various terrain conditions, the chassis can be adjusted into four different configurations.
cars.hero: A high-performance luxury car prepared as a "beautifully wrapped gift."
cars.name_long: Italdesign EXENEO Vision Gran Turismo Street Mode

cars.description: The Jaguar D-Type was a racing sports car introduced in 1954 as the successor to the C-Type, with just 64 units produced in total. It's built on a tubular frame with monocoque construction. Its sleek bodywork, penned by Malcolm Sayer, was instantly recognizable by the aerodynamic fin positioned behind the driver’s seat. It made its debut at the 1954 24 Hours of Le Mans and went on to dominate the event, securing victory three years in a row through 1957.
cars.hero: With three consecutive victories at Le Mans, this racing Jaguar featured a large fin that helped lateral stability at high speed.

cars.description: A 2-seater sports car released in 1961. Its refined stylings had a profound impact on sports car design all over the world. The 3.6L inline-6 DOHC engine produces 265.3 HP, propelling the lightweight 2687 lbs body to speeds of up to 130.5 mph. 7820 Series I models were produced, with most of them carried over to the United States.
cars.hero: The masterpiece 2-seater sports car continues to inspire car designers around the world.

cars.description: A Gran Turismo Original, Jaguar’s new-generation F-type coupe has been reimagined to comply with Gr.3 regulations. This race machine preserves the elegance of the production model’s design, while adopting a more aggressive stance with wide fenders. A key highlight is the swan-neck rear wing, extending from the tail lights, delivering both structural rigidity and increased downforce.
cars.hero: The top-of-the-line version of Jag's pure sports car has a distinctive British flair.

cars.description: A Gran Turismo Original, Jaguar’s new-generation F-type coupe has been reimagined to comply with Gr.4 regulations. This model features a bold new look, finished in matte gray with the front grille garnishes removed. Despite its styling, the car remains approachable behind the wheel, offering stable cornering and impressive straight-line performance.
cars.hero: The top-of-the-line version of Jag's pure sports car has a distinctive British flair.

cars.description: Introduced in 2012, this sports car was created as a spiritual successor to the legendary E-type, which ended production in 1975. Initially offered only as a convertible, a coupe version was added just over a year later. This particular model is the high-performance F-type R Coupé, unveiled alongside the hardtop variant. Powered by a supercharged 5.0-liter V-8 producing 542.4 HP, it could accelerate from zero to 62.1 mph in just 4.2 seconds, with an electronically limited top speed of 186.4 mph.
cars.hero: The top-of-the-line version of Jag's pure sports car has a distinctive British flair.

cars.description: This Vision Gran Turismo was created by Jaguar Advanced Design. A fully electric model, it carries forward the legacy of Jaguar’s legendary race cars like the C-type, D-type, and E-type, not only in elegance, but also in engineering, with a low center of mass and near-perfect weight distribution. Inside the cockpit, all essential driving information has been seamlessly projected ahead of the driver, delivering a thrilling racing experience through advanced digital integration.
cars.hero: This fully electric sports car combines Jaguar's rich racing tradition with the latest in EV technology.

cars.description: Jaguar’s third Vision Gran Turismo paid homage to the iconic Jaguar D-type. This futuristic electric open single-seater with an aero screen is powered by three electric motors generating more than 986.2 HP. Behind the seat is a modern take on the D-type’s signature fin, while the focused, minimalist cockpit controls reflected Jaguar’s storied racing legacy.
cars.hero: A roadster that's an heir to the legendary D-Type.

cars.description: Jaguar’s second Vision Gran Turismo was developed with engineering input from Jaguar Special Vehicles (SV). While retaining its elegant silhouette, the car received a complete aerodynamic overhaul to maximize downforce. The powertrain features four electric motors, drawing from Jaguar’s Formula E expertise. The battery system utilizes state-of-the-art liquid nitrogen cooling.
cars.hero: This virtual electric race car provides a glimpse into the future of Jaguar.

cars.description: Completed in 1966, this was Jaguar’s first mid-engine racing sports car. Its low, aerodynamic body—reminiscent of the E-type—housed a 495.1 HP 5.0-liter DOHC V-12. Although it showed great promise as a competitive circuit machine, Jaguar’s management at the time had little interest in motorsport, and the project was ultimately cancelled. Often regarded as Jaguar’s most beautiful race car, it faded into history without ever turning a wheel in competition.
cars.hero: A dream car that never came to be, this beautiful V12 mid-engine race car disappeared.

cars.description: The XJ220 was named for its record-breaking top speed, reaching 220 mph (220 mph), making it the fastest road car of its time. Production was managed by Jaguar Sport, a joint venture between Jaguar and Tom Walkinshaw Racing. It was powered by a twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V-6 derived from the XJR-11 Group C race car, mounted to a chassis constructed from aluminum honeycomb and carbon Kevlar composites. Beginning in 1993, the XJ220 also saw competition in GT racing, including entries at the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
cars.hero: A road-going Group C car with breath-taking bodywork

cars.description: Following its string of successes at Le Mans during the 1950s, Jaguar made a return to endurance racing in 1986 with a Group C prototype. Jaguar reached its peak in 1988 with the XJR-9. Thanks to its exceptional aerodynamics and durability, it claimed victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans. That triumph secured its place in motorsports history, as Jaguar dethroned Porsche, the long-reigning champions of Le Mans.
cars.hero: This iconic race car brought Jaguar many victories, notably against turbocharged competitors.

cars.description: The roots of the SUV category could be traced back to this compact 4-wheel-drive vehicle, developed at the request of the U.S. military in 1940. Among the prototypes submitted by Bantam, Ford, and Willys, it was the Willys MB—an improved version of the MA—that proved to be the winner, ultimately leading to the production of over 360,000 units. Its straightforward yet durable construction, featuring a ladder frame, rigid axles, and 4-wheel drive, resulted in a truly historic vehicle whose legacy has endured for generations.
cars.hero: The U.S. Army-commissioned vehicle that became the forefather of the modern SUV.

cars.description: The X-BOW was the first sports car developed by Austrian motorcycle manufacturer KTM. Pronounced “Crossbow,” it drew inspiration from the mechanical bow weapon that shares its name. Stripped of doors and windows, this minimalist two-seater eliminated all superfluous features in pursuit of pure performance. With its precise handling, the car was capable of sustaining up to 1.5 lateral Gs through corners.
cars.hero: The KTM X-Bow is a unique Audi turbo-powered track car from the Austrian motorcycle manufacturer.

cars.description: The original Aventador made its debut at the 2011 Geneva Motor Show, taking over from the Murciélago. Its chassis was thoroughly reengineered, now utilizing a carbon monocoque paired with aluminum subframes at both ends, replacing the steel tube frame of its predecessor. Thanks to the extensive use of carbon fiber and aluminum, the SV achieved an impressively low dry weight of just 3472 lbs for a car in this class.
cars.hero: The new flagship of the heralded supercar company was nothing short of awesome.

cars.description: Lamborghini’s flagship models had long featured V-12 engines, but their most extreme variants carried the Superveloce (SV) badge. Translated as "super fast" in Italian, the designation traced its origins back to the legendary Miura. The Aventador SV variant was introduced in 2015, delivering 49.3 HP more than the base model for a total output of 739.6 HP.
cars.hero: The top-of-the-line version of the Aventador wore the revered SV badge.

cars.description: First unveiled at the 1971 Geneva Motor Show, the Lamborghini Countach became the prototypical supercar. The first production version, the LP400, launched in 1974 in a limited run of just 150 units. In 1985, Lamborghini introduced the 5000 Quattrovalvole, powered by a 5.2-liter engine producing 448.7 HP. The final version of the Countach was the 25th Anniversary model, released in 1988, with a total production run of 657 units.
cars.hero: The final model of the Countach, commemorating the 25th anniversary of Lamborghini.

cars.description: First unveiled at the 1971 Geneva Motor Show, the Lamborghini Countach became a landmark in supercar history, drawing global attention with its groundbreaking design and performance. Named after a word from the Piedmontese dialect meaning “surprise,” the Countach lived up to its name in every sense. Marcello Gandini’s bold, near-futuristic styling left an indelible mark on the design language of high-performance cars for generations to follow.
cars.hero: The futuristic styling of this exotic car attracted quite a bit of attention from all around the world.

cars.description: Based on the Diablo GT2—a full race car built for FIA GT championships—the Diablo GT was a street-legal version that had been detuned and modified for road use. Its 6.0-liter V-12 engine produced 567.1 HP and 462.9 ft-lb of torque. Weighing in at just 3285 lbs—88 lbs lighter than the Diablo SV—the GT was capable of reaching an astonishing top speed of 210 mph.
cars.hero: The 80-car limited-edition model that was positioned as "The Ultimate Diablo."

cars.description: Released in 2008, the Lamborghini Gallardo LP 560-4 delivered a 39.4 HP boost over its predecessor. It retained the 4-wheel-drive system but introduced a new 6-speed E-gear transmission, offering gear shifts 40 percent quicker than before. Weight was also trimmed, bringing the body down to 3108 lbs, while top speed rose to 201.9 mph. With its sleek design and elevated performance, it embodied the peak of refined speed.
cars.hero: No longer a "baby Lambo," this car possessed top-tier performance.

cars.description: Lamborghini’s entry-level, mid-engine, all-wheel-drive Huracán has been reimagined as a Gr.4-spec machine for this Gran Turismo Original. Its 4-wheel-drive layout provides exceptional stability, while the balanced weight distribution of the mid-engine design delivers sharp cornering, resulting in a well-rounded and highly composed race car.
cars.hero: With aesthetics inspired by the Gallardo, this AWD supercar's powerful and lightweight nature makes it ideal for the race track.

cars.description: Unveiled in January 2015, the Huracán GT3 was a dedicated racing version of the Huracán, built to FIA GT3 specifications. While it retained the aluminum and carbon fiber hybrid construction of the road car, the body width was increased. Numerous aerodynamic enhancements were added, giving it a more aggressive and purposeful appearance.
cars.hero: Dallara took the best elements of the Huracán and created a radical competition GT3 machine.

cars.description: The Huracán was unveiled in 2014 as the replacement for the Gallardo. Its construction shifted from an aluminum space frame to a hybrid structure of aluminum and carbon fiber, resulting in a 50 percent increase in rigidity and a 10 percent reduction in weight. Positioned amidships, the 5.2-liter V-10 engine delivered 601.6 HP and 412.3 ft-lb of torque. Power was routed through a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission and sent to the pavement via the Haldex 5 all-wheel-drive system.
cars.hero: With aesthetics inspired by the Gallardo, this AWD supercar's powerful and lightweight nature makes it ideal for the race track.

cars.description: This Vision Gran Turismo concept was born from the passion and technical expertise of the team at Centro Stile Lamborghini. Built around Lamborghini’s signature design language, highlighted by bold "Y" elements and hexagonal forms, it also pays tribute to the iconic Stratos Zero with a side profile that echoed its striking silhouette. Power comes from a V-12 engine paired with a supercapacitor-based hybrid system, derived from the Sián FKP 37. In a refined detail, part of this advanced system is visible from the outside, blending high-performance engineering with unmistakable style.
cars.hero: This futuristic single-seat sports concept possesses the core concepts of Lamborghini's design DNA.

cars.description: Lamborghini’s first supercar, the Miura P400, debuted in 1966 and marked a revolutionary leap in automotive design—catapulting the brand onto the global stage. This groundbreaking machine was the result of a collaboration between industry legends: Marcello Gandini, then chief designer at Bertone; Gian Paolo Dallara, who engineered the chassis; and Paolo Stanzani, who would go on to create the Countach.
cars.hero: This car put Lamborghini on the supercar map and defined the genre.

cars.description: A high-performance evolution of Lamborghini’s flagship Murciélago made its debut in 2006. The transversely mounted V-12 engine, originally displacing 6.2 liters, was enlarged to 6.5 liters, delivering an impressive 631.2 HP. Its exterior received a comprehensive aerodynamic redesign, complemented by upgrades to the transmission and electronic systems.
cars.hero: With 631.2 HP, the flagship supercar from Lamborghini reached a top speed of 211.3 mph.

cars.description: Introduced in 2018, the Urus was Lamborghini’s high-performance SUV. It marked the brand’s first use of forced induction, powered by a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 capable of accelerating from zero to 62.1 mph in 3.6 seconds, and reaching a top speed of 189.5 mph—a record at the time of its debut. Equipped with active air suspension, rear-wheel steering, and a torque vectoring system, it delivered exceptional handling and cornering capabilities uncommon in vehicles of its class.
cars.hero: Lamborghini's take on a high-performance exotic SUV.

cars.description: The Veneno was a special limited-edition model created to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Lamborghini’s founding. Only three units were ever sold to the public. Based on the Aventador and sharing its chassis and powertrain, the Veneno featured an uprated engine producing 739.6 HP, while weight was reduced through enhancements such as a carbon-fiber monocoque. As a result, the Veneno was 276 lbs lighter than the Aventador, with a total weight of just 3197 lbs.
cars.hero: Lamborghini celebrated its 50th anniversary with this extremely limited-production super car.

cars.description: Following a dominant run of victories in the World Rally Championship, powered by the exceptional performance of the Lancia Delta, Lancia faced rising pressure from a resurgent Toyota team in 1991. In response, the marque developed the ultimate evolution of its rally icon: the HF Integrale Evoluzione. This version not only featured increased engine output but also introduced a reworked front-to-rear power distribution and significantly enhanced handling characteristics. Making its debut in the 1992 WRC season, the Evoluzione extended Lancia’s record-setting streak of consecutive championship victories.
cars.hero: This last and most potent Delta set the WRC record for consecutive wins.

cars.description: Lancia transformed the Delta into a high-performance machine by introducing 4-wheel drive and adding a turbocharger, resulting in the HF 4WD, which first appeared in the 1987 WRC Group A class. The Delta HF 4WD would later evolve into the legendary Integrale, featuring widened blister fenders and increased engine output. With each passing year, the body and suspension received significant upgrades. Thanks to these developments, the car secured eight victories during the 1992 season, earning its sixth consecutive World Rally Championship title.
cars.hero: The Lancia Delta, a six-time consecutive WRC Champion.
cars.name_long: Lancia Delta HF Integrale Rally Car '92

cars.description: In 1970, Bertone unveiled the visionary Stratos Zero. The bold, wedge-shaped concept would evolve into the production Lancia Stratos. Built on a rigid monocoque frame with lightweight fiberglass body panels, it housed a 2.4-liter DOHC V-6 engine. With its exceptionally short wheelbase and razor-sharp handling, it excelled in rally competition.
cars.hero: This mid-engine sports car made quite the impression on the rally world with its sharp wedge-shaped body.

cars.description: The LC500 is a luxury sports coupe that made its debut at the 2016 Geneva Motor Show.
